metadata.title: Week 7 Summary: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Hrishikesh. In Week seven, we tear down Anthropic's blog on redesigning source control for agent scale. From May to September 2026, daily merges jumped twelvefold from twenty-five hundred to over thirty thousand, forcing a five-month migration from git to Scion.

props.command: summarize Anthropic's engineering blog: Redesigning source control at Anthropic (Scion & Antique).
output: ✓ Migrated monorepo from git to Scion in 5 months

beats.narration_text: Coding is no longer Anthropic's bottleneck—human-scale infrastructure is. Git assumes offline clients holding full repo copies. When always-online agents and CI jobs run twenty-five million daily checkouts on a hundred-gigabyte history, naive git traffic exceeds six hundred petabytes a day.

props.text:
Hypothesis:
Git scales to any monorepo
using shallow clones and mirrors.
Wait: AI agents stay online.
At 25 million checkouts per day,
decentralized git is the bottleneck.

beats.narration_text: From January to September 2026, merges surged from twenty-five hundred per day in May to thirty thousand four hundred and one on September ninth across git pull requests and Antique change requests, leaving hundreds of git mirrors and twenty-five-gigabyte working copy seeds lagging behind main.

Inspired by Google's Piper and Meta's Sapling, Scion follows six principles: always-online clients, client-server asymmetry, full API access for zero-checkout queries, horizontal scaling without packfiles, lock-free server commits proportional to change size, and sparse or virtualized working copies.

props.command: What are the six core architectural principles behind Anthropic's Scion version control system?

beats.narration_text: A Scion changeset is a lock-free Spanner write-ahead log entry storing only file deltas against its first parent plus content-addressed pointers to compressed Cloud Storage blobs. Root trees, file blame, path history, and commit skip lists are computed recursively as derived data.

props.code:
# Spanner metadata WAL: O(change_size), lock-free
struct Changeset {
  id: "9f2c..7ab0",
  author: "Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>",
  parents: ["d41c..88e2"],
  file_changes: [
    ("docs/guide.md", Blob("3e1f..a2c4"), Regular),
    ("src/legacy.rs", Deleted),
    ("tools/build.sh", Blob("9b07..5d18"), Exec),
  ],
}
# Derived recursively: RootTree, Blame, PathHistory, SkipList

beats.narration_text: Instead of packfile negotiation, the scn client fetches missing trees and blobs across three tiers speaking identical RPCs: per-node scion-daemon, regional in-memory scion-cache, and authoritative scion-server. Over ninety-nine percent cache hit rates shrank infrastructure two hundred X and reclaimed twenty-five percent of CI CPU.

Just seven engineers built Scion, Antique, and six related systems in five months, merging twelve thousand two hundred and fifty-seven changes with Claude Mythos Preview and Claude Tag. Mythos rewrote git ingestion using twenty times less memory at four X speed, while engineers reviewed intent and told Claude no.

props.text:
7 engineers built Scion and Antique in 5 months
with 12257 changes via Claude Mythos and Tag.
Mythos rewrote the ingestion prototype:
20x less memory and 4x faster.
Engineers focus on reviewing syntax
and telling Claude no on bad patterns.

beats.narration_text: On native Scion repos, developer status drops from three point nine seconds to nineteen milliseconds—two hundred and seven times faster—and pull is twenty-five times faster. Agent worktree creation drops from seven point one minutes to five point one seconds, saving eleven thousand agent hours and two hundred eighty thousand machine hours daily.

Scion adds directory-level IAM while Antique enforces semantic approval rules. In Slack, Claude Tag superfans monitor each service's telemetry, and hermetic simulations plus post-merge automated testing replace global merge queue locks.

props.code:
# Agent-scale security, telemetry & CI
security:
  iam: directory_level_permissions
  antique_review: semantic_approval_constraints
monitoring:
  claude_tag_superfans:
    - "#scion-daemon-superfan"
    - "#scion-cache-superfan"
    - "#antique-merge-queue-superfan"
ci_workflow:
  global_merge_queue_lock: false
  strategy: post_merge_and_pre_deploy_testing

beats.narration_text: While Scion is bespoke to Anthropic's monorepo, its server-side RPCs, tree-and-blob fetch protocol, and composable sparse checkouts can scale git, GitHub, and GitLab. Try this prompt on your stack. Your turn.
